newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended lower on Monday after bund futures faltered and data from the United States confirmed the day's negative tone, dealers said.
"(Bund futures) failed to break 102 and then we had the U.S. figures. Guilder bonds slightly outperformed bunds for a while on the way down," one trader said.
The weakness was more accentuated at the longer end of the curve, although some traders the relative steadiness of shorter term paper was the result of market apathy in this area.
Despite the fall, yields were still deemed unattractive after weeks of steady bullishness. The yield on the benchmark 10 year bond, the 5.75 percent 2007, was 5.58 percent.
"(Yields) are still at a very low level," one trader said.
Some traders said the market was more interested in today's June 2002 issue from General Electric Capital Corp, albeit an issue of only 200 million guilders
"It's priced just over the curve and there's really no real supply in that area," one trader said.
Traders said U.S. figures and the Federal Market Open Committee meeting, starting Tuesday, were likely to dominate their attention in the coming days.
